facts.statement: Kerberosaurus is a saurolophine duckbill dinosaur that lived 66 million years ago in the Upper Cretaceous of Russia.
facts.quote: Kerberosaurus (meaning "Kerberos lizard") is a genus of saurolophine duckbill dinosaur from the late Maastrichtian-aged (Upper Cretaceous) Tsagayan Formation of Blagoveshchensk, Amur Region, Russia (dated to 66 million years ago).

facts.statement: A large dinosaur bonebed containing Kerberosaurus fossils was discovered in 1984 by Yuri Bolotsky and the Amur Complex Integrated Research Institute.
facts.quote: In 1984, Yuri Bolotsky and the Amur Complex Integrated Research Institute discovered a large dinosaur bonebed at Blagoveschensk.

facts.statement: Kerberosaurus is distinguished by narrow frontals, a unique braincase shape, and a distinct separation between the bone around the nostrils and the surrounding bone.
facts.quote: Diagnostic characters included narrow frontals, unique form of the braincase, and a well-demarcated division between the area of bone surrounding the nostrils and the bone outside of it.

facts.statement: Kerberosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of about 8 meters (26 feet).
facts.quote: It has been estimated to be around 8 meters (26 ft) in length.

facts.statement: Kerberosaurus was a large herbivore that walked on two or four legs and ate plants using complex dental batteries.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Kerberosaurus would have been a large bipedal\quadrupedal herbivore, consuming plant matter with complex dental batteries.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Kerberosaurus as the sister taxon to the genera Saurolophus and Prosaurolophus.
facts.quote: In their cladistic analysis, the authors found Kerberosaurus to be the sister taxon to Saurolophus and Prosaurolophus.

facts.statement: Kerberosaurus manakini is the only known species of this extinct ornithopod hadrosaur that lived in the late Cretaceous Maastrichtian, about 66 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Kerberosaurus manakini es la única especie conocida del género extinto Kerberosaurus ("lagarto de Kerberos") de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace unos 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: In 2014, Xing et al. proposed that Kundurosaurus nagornyi is a junior synonym of Kerberosaurus manakini based on shared skeletal characters and occurrence in the same formation.
facts.quote: Por otro lado, Xing et al. en 2014 consideraron a Kundurosaurus nagornyi como un sinónimo más moderno de Kerberosaurus manakini sobre la base de su coincidencia dentro de la misma formación y presencia de caracteres compartidos en sus esqueletos.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Kerberosaurus spans the Maastrichtian stage from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kerberosaurus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae and the subfamily Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Hadrosauriformes familia: Hadrosauridae subfamilia: Saurolophinae

rejected.statement: The genus Kerberosaurus was named in 2004 based on distinctive cranial material including a braincase found in a 1984 bonebed.
rejected.quote: The cranial material (holotype AENM 1/319, a braincase, and other skull bones) of the saurolophine was sufficiently distinctive to permit the naming of a new taxon, Kerberosaurus manakini, described twenty years later.
